reason: The catalyst cartridge fits the retort and is the only offered action toward building the reactor.
expectation: I expect the cartridge to be fitted into the retort, preparing it for methane production; further connections may be needed.

effect: The retort now has a clean catalyst gas path, ready to mount on the process frame.
reaction: The separate insert makes the change from ore processing feel sensible.
reason: Mounting the catalyzed retort on the frame is the only offered combination and advances the reactor assembly.
expectation: I expect the retort to be supported by the frame, with gas controls still to connect.

effect: The catalyzed retort is mounted, so gas controls are the next assembly step.
reaction: The mounting was straightforward, with no further detail.
reason: The manifold is the only offered combination and should provide the reactor's gas controls.
expectation: I expect the manifold to connect to the mounted retort; the gas supplies may still need connecting.

effect: The reactor is assembled with heating, metering and cooling controls; the next goal is to make methane.
reaction: The need to remove reaction heat as well as start the reaction is a useful detail.
reason: Connecting carbon dioxide is the only offered combination and supplies an ingredient for methane.
expectation: I expect carbon dioxide to enter the controlled reactor and react with hydrogen, producing contained methane, though further collection equipment may be needed.

effect: The carbon dioxide is coupled to the reactor; a cylinder connection remains.
reaction: The connection was straightforward, though the result gave no process detail.
reason: The gas cylinders are the only offered combination and should contain the reactor's output.
expectation: I expect the cylinders to collect methane, although additional gas separation or processing may be needed.

effect: The run produced methane, but its mixture with water vapour and unreacted gases means further processing is needed before tank use.
reaction: The qualified result was satisfying: it made the first methane feel like a test rather than instant rocket fuel.

mostWorthwhile.text: The commissioning run was most worthwhile because it produced methane while clearly explaining why the output is not yet usable as rocket fuel.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the retort was the least engaging moment: it was a straightforward required step with no explanatory detail.

surprise.text: The reactor needed cooling to remove reaction heat as well as heating to start it.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the sequence was entirely dictated by the single offered combination at each step.

continue.text: Yes. I would like to see how the mixed output is processed for the return trip; the final test made that next problem concrete.
